verdicts.verify_by: cp reviews/pr/6xxx/6196-cur-binding-holes/1-6d88deba7/tests/b1-tests-r2-shadow-readback.gno to gnovm/tests/files/zz_cur_shadow_readback.gno and run go test ./gnovm/pkg/gnolang/ -run 'TestFiles/zz_cur_shadow_readback.gno$' -v; then read gnovm/tests/files/zrealm_cur_shadow.gno lines 11-20 for the absent read-back
verdicts.tldr: the fixture that newly legalises rebinding a realm-typed shadow never reads the parameter back, so a runtime aliasing regression leaves it green
verdicts.details: zrealm_cur_shadow.gno writes the shadow four ways inside an inner block and then ends on println("ok") with no mention of cur after the closing brace, so the only thing it asserts is that the block preprocesses. Its static half is self-pinning: if the shadow resolved to the parameter, isCrossingCurParam would panic at preprocess and the fixture would go red. What nothing pins is the runtime half, a slot that statically reads block-scoped while aliasing the parameter's heap item: `*p = nil` would then null main's frame identity and every assertion in the file still passes. Fix: add one read of cur after the block, which the finder's file shows printing true at head.
verdicts.evidence: gnovm/tests/files/zrealm_cur_shadow.gno lines 11-19: the block runs `cur := cur; cur = nil; p := &cur; *p = nil; _ = cur`, then line 19 is `println("ok")` and line 21-22 are `// Output:` / `// ok`. No line between the closing brace and the end of main names cur. The read-back probe under tests/ is the discriminating assertion and passes at head, so the gap is coverage only.

verdicts.verify_by: read preprocess.go:6112 and 6121 against the provenance switch's default arm; any node kind added to GetBlockNodeForPath changes one site's answer and not the other's
verdicts.tldr: the two defaults are opposite by design for every node kind that exists; only a third function-shaped block node would reopen the hole
verdicts.details: The asymmetry is real and read-settled, but it is correct for every kind GetBlockNodeForPath returns today: a package-level `var cur realm` resolves to a FileNode or PackageNode, where writable and not-cur-callable are both the right answers, so one arm must fail open and the other closed. The residual risk is narrower than the finder states: adding a third function-shaped BlockNode kind would silently return false from isCrossingCurParam while the provenance switch loudly panics. The godoc's claim that the two are "the same declaration test" is what is inaccurate, and a finding on a comment's wording ships SKIP. Fix: word the godoc to say the two arms share a lookup and not a verdict, and confirming the behavioural half needs a third function-shaped node kind, which no branch has.
verdicts.evidence: preprocess.go:6115-6122 switches *FuncDecl and *FuncLitExpr then `return false`; preprocess.go:2156-2177 switches the same two then `default: panic("only the `cur` argument of a containing crossing function maybe passed by cross-call")`. preprocess.go:6107-6110 claims "This is the same declaration test the cur-call provenance check makes".

verdicts.tldr: preprocess permitting the shape and the runtime refusing the cross-frame use is the designed split, pinned by a fixture
verdicts.details: The preprocess NOTE and the reworded runtime comment govern different axes: the NOTE says a captured cur cannot outlive its frame across transactions and is a valid handle to its own frame's authority within one, while the runtime text refuses a capture forwarded from a different frame. "Preprocesses cleanly and aborts at runtime" is not a contradiction here, it is the invariant the project deliberately keeps, and a filetest asserts the exact panic text for it. The candidate is in any case about a comment's own wording, which changes no behaviour. Fix: none.

verdicts.verify_by: Delete the `if n.Op != DEFINE {` wrapper at preprocess.go:3100 and run go test ./gnovm/pkg/gnolang/ -run 'TestFiles$' -short: no new failure, since `for cur := range xs` inside a crossing function defines in the RangeStmt block.
verdicts.tldr: the surviving DEFINE carve-out cannot change any outcome, so one rule now reads two ways across two sites
verdicts.details: RangeStmt is a BlockNode whose init block is pushed before the key and value are defined, and the DEFINE'd names are reserved against the RangeStmt itself as declaring node. isCrossingCurParam switches only on *FuncDecl and *FuncLitExpr, so a range DEFINE always answers false and the guard body would be a no-op with the wrapper gone. The assign guard at 3011 dropped the same carve-out this PR, on the premise that a DEFINE can be a rebind; the next reader has to redo the block-push argument to see that the surviving one is not a second hole of the kind fix 1 closed. The read settles it without the mutation the finder proposed. Fix: drop the wrapper, or state in the comment that the carve-out is redundant rather than load-bearing.
